On 6-17-2015, I signed up for an account with PayPal in order to make a donation to hello@voat.co (Voat). On 6-18-2015, my bank listed a withdrawal in the amount of the donation plus applicable fees.

Today, though, Voat posted news that their PayPal account has been frozen due to content that your company has deemed objectionable. There are a couple of problems with this:

  1. Voat.co does not host the content. They link to content that is hosted elsewhere. Only text posts may be hosted on the site itself. The objectionable content you used as reason for the freeze is not on Voat's servers.

  2. As your company may or may not be aware, the reason that the objectionable content was pointed out to you was due to a dispute between users of the sites reddit.com and voat.co. Reddit, also, hosts links to outside content, and much of it is, also, objectionable. The difference is that reddit, unlike Voat, has a system known as reddit Gold, whereby users can reward each other for posting links to this content - and one method of payment for reddit Gold is PayPal. This means that your company is directly responsible for funding links to this content, in forums as varied as reddit.com/r/beatingwomen, reddit.com/r/coontown, and reddit.com/r/deadbabies; whereas on Voat, PayPal has only been handling transactions given by users to the developers of the site, who are not profiting from these donations, but using it to purchase server time and equipment to increase the capacity of the site.

As a result, there are two reasonable and logical courses of action.

The first, and the preferable, is that your company realizes that neither reddit nor Voat is directly hosting this content, and that your company should have no liability in the matter. In this case, your company would unfreeze Voat.co's account, and continue to enjoy the profits that come from the fees of many people's continued donations to the site. I would enjoy seeing confirmation that my own donation has gone through, as well, and would continue to offer my trust to PayPal in providing transaction services to me.

The second is that should your company decide that Voat is indeed "hosting" objectionable content, that you will also recognize that not only does reddit also "host" the same types of content, but that it does so on a vastly larger scale, and that it does so by rewarding users with purchased rewards - for which your company provides transactions. In this case, in order to retain a sense of fairness and, indeed, to remove any semblance of legal liability for unfair application of your rules, you should also freeze all funds and transactions related to any accounts associated with reddit.com and its parent company, Advance Publications. In the event that you choose this route, it would also be prudent to refund the donations of the hundreds of Voat users who, in good faith, used PayPal's services to assist in supporting Voat's development as a new and burgeoning platform. I would also enjoy seeing my own donation be refunded, if it will not be made available to Voat - and if I receive a refund while reading of the freezing of reddit's accounts, I will accept my refund with no ill will towards PayPal.

Of course, there is a third route, which is neither reasonable nor logical. In this route, you continue to freeze Voat's account while leaving reddit's untouched. As a result, I, and I am sure hundreds of other Voat users whose donations have been frozen, will look forward to a refund, and failing that, will consider terminating our accounts and any further transactions with your company, while considering our legal options both under the PayPal User Agreement and outside of it.

In brief, I wish to know which route PayPal intends to take: 1) Whether they will remove the freeze on hello@voat.co or institute one on accounts related to reddit.com; and 2) Should the freeze on hello@voat.co remain, whether PayPal users who sent funds should expect a refund, and if so, in what time frame can it be expected.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
